clues.text: This seaside town sits on the coast of England. It stands where the Humber river flows into the sea.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside the coast of England

source.quote: Cleethorpes () is a seaside town on the estuary of the Humber in North East Lincolnshire, Lincolnshire, England with a population of 29,670 in 2021.

clues.text: Rain falls here less than in most places. Its yearly rainfall is among the lowest in the British Isles.
clues.narrowing: rules out the wetter parts of the British Isles

source.quote: The town lies on the prime meridian, also known as the Greenwich meridian, and its average annual rainfall is amongst the lowest in the British Isles.

clues.text: People have lived here since the 6th century. Fishing was its first trade, long before holiday crowds came.
clues.narrowing: rules out newer resorts with no long fishing past

source.quote: It has been permanently occupied since the 6th century, with fishing as its original industry, and then developing into a resort in the 19th century.

clues.text: In 2021, its beach earned high praise. A train company ranked it second best among seaside spots trains can reach.
clues.narrowing: rules out almost every other British seaside town

source.quote: In 2021, Trainline named Cleethorpes beach the second best seaside destination in the UK that is reachable by train, just behind Margate.

clues.text: This town stands on the prime meridian line. The line is also called the Greenwich meridian.
clues.narrowing: rules out every town not on the Greenwich meridian line

source.quote: The town lies on the prime meridian, also known as the Greenwich meridian, and its average annual rainfall is amongst the lowest in the British Isles.

clues.text: This capital city sits in Galicia, in the northwest of Spain. Picture the top left corner of the map of Spain.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside northwest Spain

source.quote: Santiago de Compostela, alternatively abbreviated to Santiago or Compostela, is the capital of the autonomous community of Galicia, Spain. It is located in the province of A Coruña, in the northwest of the Iberian Peninsula.

clues.text: Winters here are mild, but the rain is heavy. Atlantic storm winds push that rain in from the ocean.
clues.narrowing: rules out dry inland Spain and cold northern places

source.quote: Santiago de Compostela has a very mild climate for its latitude with heavy winter rainfall courtesy of its relative proximity to the prevailing winds from Atlantic low-pressure systems.

clues.text: This city began with a shrine to Saint James the Great. Pilgrims have walked here since the 9th century.
clues.narrowing: rules out places with no ancient pilgrimage shrine

source.quote: The city has its origin in the shrine of Saint James the Great, now the Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela, as the destination of the Way of St. James, a leading Catholic pilgrimage route since the 9th century.

clues.text: Its old town is so special that UNESCO protects it. It joined the World Heritage list in 1985.
clues.narrowing: rules out all but a few protected old towns in Spain

source.quote: In 1985, the city's Old Town was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

clues.text: Its grand cathedral is the end of the Way of Saint James. Walkers finish their journey at this famous church.
clues.narrowing: confirms the pilgrimage capital of Galicia
